recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla confirms voice-taught FSD context; Grok→planning by September
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 8, 2026, Tesla VP of AI Software Ashok Elluswamy confirmed Tesla is building a feature that lets drivers teach the car hyper-local context in plain language (e.g. which driveway) with the instruction remembered for future trips. Elon Musk separately confirmed Grok voice commands will pass into FSD's planning layer by September 2026. This is infrastructure for both consumer FSD and robotaxi last-mile pickup quality, but remains unreleased pending safety testing.

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla confirms FSD v15 delayed to end-2026/early-2027; robotaxi scale blocked until release
recentKeyChanges.description: During the Q1 2026 earnings call (April 22, 2026), Tesla confirmed FSD v15 will not ship until late 2026 or early 2027, representing a delay of the 10x parameter model upgrade that was originally planned for v14 in late 2025. CEO Elon Musk explicitly stated large-scale robotaxi expansion will NOT proceed until v15 is released, citing the need for 'major architectural improvements' to reach required safety levels. This confirms v15 is the critical blocker for both unsupervised FSD and robotaxi commercialization. The 10-billion-parameter model is described as a 'total architectural overhaul' designed to achieve 'orders of magnitude beyond human capability' safety. While v15 will run on Hardware 4 (no upgrade needed), the ~9-12 month delay from original v14 timeline pushes Tesla's autonomy roadmap into 2027.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Headlines emphasize HW4 compatibility (positive framing), but reality is a 9-12 month delay of the critical model upgrade, pushing robotaxi scale and unsupervised FSD into 2027. This is the second major delay (originally v14 late-2025, now v15 end-2026/early-2027). Robotaxi expansion explicitly blocked until v15 ships.

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla confirms Hardware 3 cannot support unsupervised FSD or v15; 4M vehicles left behind
recentKeyChanges.description: On April 22-23, 2026 (Q1 earnings call), Tesla officially confirmed that Hardware 3 (HW3) vehicles—approximately 4 million globally—cannot and will not support unsupervised Full Self-Driving or FSD v15. Elon Musk cited hardware limitations: HW3 has 'only one eighth of the memory bandwidth of Hardware 4' and lacks the compute/memory capacity for the 10-billion-parameter v15 model. FSD v14 Lite is confirmed as the 'ultimate ceiling version' for HW3 hardware. This directly contradicts Tesla's 2016-2019 promises that HW3 would support full autonomy. Tesla is offering affected customers (many who paid $8,000-15,000 for FSD) either: (1) discounted trade-in to HW4 vehicle, or (2) paid hardware upgrade requiring replacement of computer AND all cameras. This represents a broken promise to millions of early FSD adopters and a material limitation on Tesla's addressable autonomy market.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Official confirmation that 4 million HW3 customers cannot access unsupervised FSD or v15 despite paying for 'Full Self-Driving' with promises of future autonomy. This is a broken commitment and requires expensive upgrades. Headlines frame it as 'upgrade path offered' but reality is customers must pay more after already purchasing FSD.
